applicability: Valid for arithmetic expressions over nonnegative integer literals in bases 2-36 using addition, multiplication, parentheses, and optional implicit multiplication (e.g., '3(1+3)'). Rejects malformed input, unsupported characters, unbalanced parentheses, and expressions longer than 100000 characters. Does not support subtraction, division, exponentiation, or negative literals.
description: Tokenize the expression into integers, '+', '*', and parentheses, then evaluate with a recursive-descent parser: parse_expr sums terms, parse_term multiplies factors (supporting explicit '*' and optional implicit multiplication by juxtaposition), and parse_factor handles integer literals in the given base and parenthesized subexpressions. Exact Python integer arithmetic is used, so nesting depth is handled mechanically. Uncertainty: tokenization assumes only '+', '*', parentheses, whitespace, and base-appropriate digits; other operators or malformed parentheses raise ValueError.
